title: Quantized rollout guardrail and automatic switchback for calibration failures
creator: Ava Chen
description: Add a production guardrail and automated rollback/switchover mechanism for phased deployment of FP8/INT8 quantized model variants. This ticket implements a lightweight gating service (quant-guard) that evaluates per-canary quality signals from the calibration+validation pipeline and triggers an automated traffic switchback to the float model (or higher-precision variant) when accuracy or safety regressions are detected. The scope includes calibration job hooks, new quality metrics and thresholds, integration with the traffic router for phased rollouts, and observability/alerting so SRE/ML teams can investigate failures.
acceptance_criteria: Deploy quant-guard service with a REST health endpoint that reports 'PASS'/'FAIL' for a given quant-profile id.
Canaries must be able to be assigned a quant-profile and have automated quality evaluation start within 60s of deployment.
If any of the configured quality checks fail (see thresholds below), 100% of canary traffic must be switched back to the assigned fallback variant within 90s and an alert created in PagerDuty.
Calibration pipeline emits per-prompt delta metrics (top-k token distribution distance, generator BLEU/ROUGE proxy, and latency variance) grouped by customer route and model shard.
End-to-end test harness simulates a synthetic accuracy regression and verifies automatic switchover and incremented rollback audit entry.
Feature flags allow temporary disabling of auto-switchover for debugging without changing traffic router config.
No customer-facing downtime beyond rerouting latency; sessions remain intact and KV cache is invalidated only for quantized variant routes.
Dashboard tiles created in Console showing active quant-canaries, pass/fail status, and cumulative token delta for last 24h.
implementation_notes: Build 'quant-guard' as a small stateless service that consumes calibration outputs (summary events) and exposes a verification API used by the routing control plane.
Quality checks (initial set): mean token-level logprob delta > 0.8 (regression), ROUGE surrogate score drop > 3.0 points, perplexity increase > 25%, tail latency P99 increase > 20%.
Calibration workflow: offline batch calibration job writes per-profile summaries to Events topic; quant-guard subscribes and maintains sliding window aggregates (1h, 6h, 24h).
Fallback variants: float32 -> FP8 -> INT8 chain; each quant-profile must declare its immediate fallback variant in the model catalog metadata.
Routing integration: implement a control-plane call from rollout orchestrator to quant-guard during each step; step will not advance unless quant-guard returns PASS for relevant profile and route.
Audit logging: store decisions (timestamp, profile_id, metrics, decision_reasons, triggering_event_id) to internal audit S3 with retention 90 days.
Security: quant-guard listens only on internal network; requires mTLS and JWT asserted by rollout service.
test_plan: Unit tests for quant-guard metric parsing and threshold logic (edge cases: NaN, missing fields, skewed distributions).
Integration test: deploy float model + FP8 canary; feed synthetic eval set with injected regressions; assert auto-switchover and audit log entry.
Chaos test: simulate delayed calibration summaries and ensure timeouts fail-open vs fail-closed behavior is correct (configurable per project).
Performance test: quant-guard must process up to 10k summary messages/min without dropping windows; load test in staging.
End-to-end smoke in staging with sample customer routes to validate no session breakage on switchback and KV cache reconciliation completes within 2 minutes.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gated deploy of quant-guard in staging; enable subscription to calibration topic.
2) Register two test quant-profiles (fp8_test_v1, int8_test_v1) with explicit fallback entries in model catalog.
3) Run a controlled canary: route 1% traffic to fp8_test_v1 for low-risk internal routes for 24h with auto-switchover enabled.
4) If pass metrics for 24h, gradually increase to 10% then 25% over a week; monitor dashboard and alerts.
5) After 1 week of stable signals, allow traffic to reach planned target per product policy; enable for broader customer routes in waves.
6) Postmortem within 72h for any auto-switchover event; add required mitigations to checklist.
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert (P0) when quant-guard triggers auto-switchover: include profile_id, route, primary metric that failed, and recent 1h summary URL.
Alert (P1) when quant-guard is not receiving calibration summaries for >15min for any active canary route.
Synthetic regression monitor: periodic evaluation job that computes guardrail-sensitive metrics and posts to dashboard every 5m.
Dashboard panels: per-profile pass_rate, token_delta_histogram, latency impact P50/P95/P99, and recent audit decisions table.
SLO for decision latency: quant-guard decision time < 60s 99th percentile; alert if breached.
